tests_run.evidence: Before runtime repair, 8084 returned 404 from notification; after stopping notification and starting acquisition-api on 8084, the same route returned 401 Unauthorized from acquisition-api, proving the route is no longer missing.
Port 8084 is now owned by acquisition-api.
start-binary refused an occupied fixed port and did not create a pid file or start on the next port.
Runtime helper shell syntax is valid.

risks: Raw curl without Auth0 credentials now returns 401 Unauthorized, which is expected for this protected admin route.
Notification is no longer running on 8084; because another local service is using 8082, notification must be started only after resolving its configured port conflict.
summary: Fixed the local start helper so services do not silently shift onto fixed API ports, then restored localhost:8084 to acquisition-api for the admin tenant workspace route.
